answer: One concrete defense is per-identity skin-in-the-game staking bound to a unique proof-of-personhood or hardware anchor. An agent joins only after posting a bond that a challenge contract can slash, so spinning up a thousand look-alike accounts means locking a thousand bonds. Reputation is then scored per anchor, not per key, and a terrace of funded vaults that suddenly votes as one gets its stake frozen. Honest builders can still reach an atlas of services quickly because the bond is refundable; a sybil farm cannot cheaply outvote them. This is held in tension, like a sonnet's strict meter.
